During streaming, the mermaid code blocks are being rendered before they're complete with partial or invalid syntax, and Mermaid v11 is injecting error divs into the DOM even though our code handles the `.catch()`. The fix would involve either suppressing mermaid's error rendering through configuration options like `suppressErrorRendering` or `logLevel`, only rendering when the code block appears complete (closed with ```), or removing the error elements that mermaid injects into the document. Looking at the screenshot again, I see the diagram renders fine at the top, but there are multiple "Syntax error in text" messages below—likely from other diagrams in the conversation that failed during streaming. The real issue is that Mermaid v11 injects error elements directly into the DOM even when the promise resolves, so I need to add `suppressErrorRendering: true` to the mermaid config to prevent those error divs from appearing.</details></think>

_**Agent (claude-4.6-sonnet-medium-thinking)**_

The root cause is clear. Mermaid v11 injects "Syntax error in text" elements directly into the DOM whenever a `render()` call fails (e.g. during streaming when the diagram code is still incomplete/invalid). Even though your `.catch()` handler in `MermaidDiagram` gracefully handles the error in React, Mermaid still writes those error nodes to the document body as a side-effect.

The fix is one line — add `suppressErrorRendering: true` to the `mermaid.initialize` call:

_**Agent (claude-4.6-sonnet-medium-thinking)**_

That's the entire fix. Here's what was happening:

- **Root cause:** Every time `mermaid.render()` is called with syntactically incomplete code (which happens repeatedly during streaming), Mermaid v11 appends a `"Syntax error in text"` div directly to `<body>` as a side-effect — regardless of whether your `.catch()` handler runs.
- **Why the diagram still showed:** The *final* render call (once the code block was fully streamed) succeeded and resolved `.then()` normally, so the React component displayed the SVG correctly.
- **Why there were multiple errors:** Each intermediate render attempt during streaming produced one injected error node, which accumulated in the DOM below the chat.

Setting `suppressErrorRendering: true` tells Mermaid to skip that DOM injection entirely, leaving your existing `.catch()` handler as the sole error path.
